summary: Iter97 verified BUG 1 (guidelines-loop) and BUG 2 (finance-repopulation). Backend 3/3 pytest pass. UI-verified BUG 2 end-to-end (tiles disappear on OFF, REPOPULATE on ON after dashboard reload). CRITICAL REGRESSION FOUND & FIXED IN DASHBOARD: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/dashboard.tsx lines 57-58 referenced `data` BEFORE its useState declaration on line 65 => Temporal Dead Zone ReferenceError 'Cannot access data before initialization' that crashed the dashboard for every user (owner + member). E1's BUG 2 patch was the trigger. Testing agent moved the two `canExpenses/canTravel` lines to immediately AFTER `const [data, setData] = useState<Dashboard|null>(null);` and restarted expo — dashboard now renders, tile-this-month/tile-paid-ytd/tile-raised/dashboard-balance-card all mount correctly. Bug 1 UI could not be exercised on web because react-native-web `Alert.alert` is a no-op (does not render a browser dialog), but code review of submit(skipGuard) + promptGuidelines(()=>submit(true)) confirms the closure-loop is broken correctly (skipGuard=true on the retry bypasses the guard) and the backend contract POST /reviews returns 403 guidelines_not_accepted BEFORE and 200 with {place_id, review_id} AFTER POST /reviews/accept-guidelines — both verified by pytest.

BUG 1 UI verification on native: react-native-web's Alert.alert is a no-op on the Metro web preview, so the guidelines popup cannot be exercised in the web preview. Verify on iOS/Android (Expo Go or a native build) that (a) a single 'Community Guidelines' popup appears on first Post review, (b) tapping 'I Agree' immediately submits and navigates to /reviews/{place_id}, and (c) the popup does NOT re-appear. critical_code_review_comments: backend/routers/reviews.py: _require_guidelines correctly gates POST /reviews with 403 detail 'guidelines_not_accepted' when reviews_guidelines_accepted_at is missing; accept-guidelines writes utcnow_iso() timestamp; /reviews/categories returns guidelines_accepted flag which new.tsx reads to seed local state.

backend/routers/dashboard.py: correctly reads visibility via _member_visibility and zeroes total_expenses_ytd/total_payments_ytd/booking_balance/unpaid_expense_balance/month_spend when the corresponding flag is false; also returns can_view_expenses/can_view_travel booleans that the UI now gates on.

frontend/app/reviews/new.tsx: submit(skipGuard=false) + `if (!skipGuard && !guidelinesAccepted) { promptGuidelines(()=>submit(true)); return; }` correctly avoids the previous stale-closure loop; onPress={() => submit()} always starts with skipGuard=false; the 'I Agree' onPress calls accept-guidelines then invokes the `after` callback which now uses submit(true). Look reasonable.

frontend/app/(tabs)/dashboard.tsx: after ordering fix, canExpenses/canTravel derive from data.can_view_expenses ?? user.visibility.expenses (falls back to auth-cache before first fetch resolves). load() calls refreshUser() so the Expenses tab (which is gated on the cached auth visibility) re-appears on re-enable too. Good.

The refreshUser() inside load() and useFocusEffect(load) means every dashboard focus performs a full /auth/me + /dashboard + /reminders round-trip. Fine here, but if Team Hub adds more focus-driven refetches, consider debouncing.

rca_of_issue: BUG 2 fix (E1) introduced a TDZ ReferenceError in dashboard.tsx by placing `const canExpenses = (data?.can_view_expenses ?? user?.visibility?.expenses) !== false;` on line 57 while `const [data, setData] = useState<Dashboard|null>(null);` sits on line 65. JavaScript hoists `const` bindings into the TDZ, so reading `data` before its declaration throws 'Cannot access data before initialization'. This crashed DashboardScreen for every user (visible in the browser via a red overlay 'Uncaught Error: Cannot access data before initialization' with stack app/(tabs)/dashboard.tsx:57:23). Mitigation: move the two derived-flag consts to immediately after the useState line so `data` is already initialised to null when they read it. After fix, dashboard renders, member privacy toggles correctly hide (OFF: month=0/paid=0/raised=0) and repopulate (ON: month=1/paid=1/raised=1) on reload.
